frame_account_level.granularity: ACCOUNT-LEVEL — same across every move (gap: not per-move yet)

frame_permove.granularity: move-level (per-move frame reader; veers measured vs account baseline)

moves.label: M1
moves.paraphrase: Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb at first-light on day one of the week, while it is still dark.
moves.substrate: the tomb
moves.outcome: Mary is at the tomb at pre-dawn
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community narrating the tomb-discovery it received as founding testimony
moves.paradigm: empty-tomb tradition / grief-visit to burial site at dawn

lineage.source_ref: Genesis 1:1-5 (day one, light out of darkness)
lineage.seam: Is 'day one of the week, while it was still dark' echoing Genesis's 'day one' before the separation of light from darkness? If so, the text

moves.label: M2
moves.paraphrase: Mary sees that the burial-stone is no longer sealing the tomb.
moves.substrate: the state of the tomb (i.e. the embedded state-of-affairs M3)
moves.outcome: Mary comes to know the tomb is open
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community narrating a first-witness perception at dawn
moves.paradigm: see-that / perception-with-propositional-complement; empty-tomb discovery

moves.label: M3
moves.paraphrase: The stone that sealed the tomb has been taken away.
moves.substrate: the sealing-stone
moves.outcome: the tomb is unsealed / open
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the un-named agent is a deliberate narrative feature
moves.paradigm: empty-tomb tradition — the who-moved-the-stone is left open

moves.label: M4
moves.paraphrase: Mary runs from the tomb and goes to Simon Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved.
moves.substrate: her own body / the path to the two disciples
moves.outcome: Mary reaches Peter and the beloved disciple
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the beloved-disciple identifier is a Johannine narrator-signature
moves.paradigm: witness-carrying / alarm-run

moves.label: M5
moves.paraphrase: Mary tells the two disciples the following.
moves.substrate: the utterance-content she conveys (embedded moves M6 and M7)
moves.outcome: Peter and the beloved disciple receive her report
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community's memory of Mary's first-report to the male disciples
moves.paradigm: reported speech; alarm-report of missing body

moves.label: M6
moves.paraphrase: Some unspecified 'they' have taken the Lord out of the tomb.
moves.substrate: 'the Lord' (Jesus's body, as Mary names him)
moves.outcome: the Lord is no longer in the tomb
moves.sitz: narrated dawn at the tomb; Mary's default explanation-frame for an empty burial
moves.paradigm: body-theft / grave-desecration as the intuitive first explanation before resurrection is available

moves.label: M7
moves.paraphrase: Mary and her group do not know the place where the Lord's body has been put.
moves.substrate: the location of the Lord's body (the embedded LAY-move M8)
moves.outcome: the location is opaque to them
moves.sitz: narrated dawn at tomb; Mary reports the group's ignorance to the two male disciples
moves.paradigm: grief-search / where-is-the-body opacity

moves.label: M8
moves.paraphrase: The unspecified 'they' have laid the Lord's body in some place.
moves.substrate: the Lord's body ('him')
moves.outcome: the body is at some location unknown to Mary
moves.sitz: narrated dawn at tomb; the presupposed act behind the not-knowing
moves.paradigm: body-theft/relocation scenario

moves.label: M9
moves.paraphrase: Peter and the beloved disciple leave and head toward the tomb together.
moves.substrate: themselves / the road to the tomb
moves.outcome: the two are on the way to the tomb, running together
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community narrating the confirmatory male-disciple visit that follows Mary's alarm
moves.paradigm: alarm-response / confirmatory visit by second and third witness

moves.label: M10
moves.paraphrase: The beloved disciple outpaces Peter on the way.
moves.substrate: Peter (the one outpaced)
moves.outcome: the beloved disciple is ahead of Peter
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the ordering of the two witnesses matters to the community's self-understanding vis-à-vis Petrine tradition
moves.paradigm: two-witness ordering; Johannine framing of beloved-disciple priority

moves.label: M11
moves.paraphrase: The beloved disciple arrives at the tomb before Peter does.
moves.substrate: the tomb
moves.outcome: the beloved disciple is at the tomb before Peter
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the first-arrival is remembered and marked
moves.paradigm: witness-ordering / arrival at the empty site

moves.label: M12
moves.paraphrase: The beloved disciple stoops down at the entrance in order to look inside.
moves.substrate: his own body / the tomb-entrance
moves.outcome: he is positioned to see into the tomb
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community narrating the disciple's threshold hesitation
moves.paradigm: threshold / hesitation-at-the-tomb-mouth

moves.label: M13
moves.paraphrase: From that stooped position he sees the linen wrappings inside.
moves.substrate: the state inside the tomb (the embedded state M14)
moves.outcome: the beloved disciple perceives the wrappings-as-lying
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the wrappings-detail is a Johannine evidentiary feature
moves.paradigm: empty-tomb evidence — grave-clothes remaining

moves.label: M14
moves.paraphrase: The linen burial-wrappings are lying inside the tomb.
moves.substrate: the linen wrappings
moves.outcome: the wrappings persist in their in-tomb position
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the-wrappings-remain evidentiary detail
moves.paradigm: grave-clothes-left-behind — signature of non-theft

moves.label: M15
moves.paraphrase: The beloved disciple, however, does not enter the tomb.
moves.substrate: the tomb interior (declined)
moves.outcome: the beloved disciple stays outside
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the deferral to Peter for first entry is a narratively-marked reticence
moves.paradigm: threshold-refrained; deferring first-entry

moves.label: M16
moves.paraphrase: Simon Peter arrives after him at the tomb.
moves.substrate: his own path / the tomb-approach
moves.outcome: Peter reaches the tomb, second
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community narrating the second-arrival
moves.paradigm: witness-ordering

moves.label: M17
moves.paraphrase: Peter goes on into the tomb.
moves.substrate: the tomb interior
moves.outcome: Peter is inside the tomb
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the who-enters-first is remembered
moves.paradigm: first-entry by Peter after the beloved disciple's deferral

moves.label: M18
moves.paraphrase: From inside, Peter sees the burial-wrappings and, separately, the head-cloth.
moves.substrate: the state inside the tomb (the embedded states M19 and M20)
moves.outcome: Peter perceives the two distinct textile arrangements
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the separation of head-cloth from body-wrappings is a Johannine evidentiary detail
moves.paradigm: empty-tomb evidence — orderly grave-clothes rule out theft

moves.label: M19
moves.paraphrase: The linen burial-wrappings are lying inside the tomb.
moves.substrate: the linen wrappings
moves.outcome: the wrappings remain in position
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; second confirmation of the wrappings-state
moves.paradigm: grave-clothes-left-behind

moves.label: M20
moves.paraphrase: The cloth that had covered Jesus's head is not with the other wrappings; it has been rolled up and set apart in its own spot.
moves.agent: not-stated (the rolling and setting-apart imply an unspecified agent)
moves.substrate: the head-cloth
moves.outcome: the head-cloth is in a rolled, separated arrangement
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the orderly separation is remembered as significant
moves.paradigm: orderly-departure signature (against body-theft, which would leave disarray)

moves.label: M21
moves.paraphrase: The beloved disciple now also enters the tomb.
moves.substrate: the tomb interior
moves.outcome: the beloved disciple is inside
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the beloved disciple's delayed entry is remembered
moves.paradigm: threshold-crossed after Peter

moves.label: M22
moves.paraphrase: Once inside, the beloved disciple sees.
moves.substrate: not-stated (the seeing is used absolutely, without a named object)
moves.outcome: the beloved disciple takes in what is there
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the absolute 'saw' is a Johannine narrative choice
moves.paradigm: inarticulate-perception preceding faith; sign-reading

moves.label: M23
moves.paraphrase: And he came to trust / hold-as-true.
moves.substrate: not-stated (the belief is used absolutely, without a named content)
moves.outcome: a state of faith / trust is established in him
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; 'to believe' absolutely is a Johannine theological signature
moves.paradigm: sign-triggered faith; the beloved disciple as exemplary faith-figure

moves.label: M24
moves.paraphrase: The narrator adds an aside: as of that moment the disciples had not yet grasped the scripture-testimony bearing on this event.
moves.substrate: the scripture (whose content is the embedded proposition M25)
moves.outcome: the interpretive frame is missing for them at that time
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community reading its founding tradition retrospectively, marking a not-yet that the community has since resolved
moves.paradigm: Johannine misunderstanding-motif; post-Easter scripture-fulfillment schema applied retrospectively

lineage.seam: The narrator invokes 'the scripture' as the necessary interpretive frame for the empty tomb, but leaves unsaid WHICH scripture — the citatio

moves.label: M25
moves.paraphrase: According to that scripture, it is necessary for Jesus to rise from among the dead.
moves.substrate: the state of being dead
moves.outcome: he rises out of the dead
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community's scripture-fulfillment reading of the resurrection
moves.paradigm: prophetic-necessity ('dei') / resurrection as scripture-fulfilled

lineage.seam: The δεῖ ('it is necessary') paraphrases an unnamed scriptural warrant as a compulsion binding on Jesus personally to rise from the dead, but

moves.label: M26
moves.paraphrase: The two male disciples then head back to where they are staying.
moves.agent: the disciples (Peter and the beloved disciple)
moves.substrate: themselves / the road back
moves.outcome: they are back at their lodgings
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the two-witness confirmation is complete and the narrative pivots back to Mary
moves.paradigm: witness-visit closed; departure

moves.label: M27
moves.paraphrase: Mary, unlike them, remains outside the tomb, on her feet, weeping.
moves.substrate: her own body-in-grief at the tomb-mouth
moves.outcome: Mary persists at the site in a standing-and-weeping posture
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; Mary's persistence-at-the-site is a marked contrast to the male disciples' departure
moves.paradigm: grief-persistence / mourner staying at the tomb

moves.label: M28
moves.paraphrase: In the middle of her weeping, Mary stoops down at the entrance to look inside the tomb.
moves.substrate: her own body / the tomb-mouth
moves.outcome: Mary is positioned to see into the tomb
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; Mary's stoop mirrors the earlier male-disciple stoop
moves.paradigm: threshold-look / bending to peer in

moves.label: M29
moves.paraphrase: From that stooped position she sees two white-robed angels inside the tomb.
moves.substrate: the interior scene of the tomb (the embedded state M30)
moves.outcome: Mary perceives the two angelic figures at the body's former place
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; angelophany at the empty tomb is a shared tradition across the resurrection accounts
moves.paradigm: angelophany at empty tomb; heavenly interpreters of the empty burial place

moves.label: M30
moves.paraphrase: Two angels dressed in white are seated at the exact spot where the body had lain, one where the head had been, the other where the feet had been.
moves.agent: not-stated (their seated presence is described, not their sitting-down act)
moves.substrate: the two angels in white / the head-and-foot positions of the former body-site
moves.outcome: the angels occupy the head and foot positions of the vacated body-place
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the head-and-foot arrangement is a marked, iconic tableau
moves.paradigm: angelophany at empty tomb; symbolic tableau flanking the absent body

lineage.source_ref: Exodus 25:17-22 (the two cherubim at the ends of the kapporet)
lineage.seam: Is the text staging the empty burial-slab as a kapporet, with two angelic figures at head and foot echoing the two cherubim bracketing the m

moves.label: M31
moves.paraphrase: The two angels address Mary with the following.
moves.substrate: the utterance-content they convey to Mary (embedded move M32)
moves.outcome: Mary is addressed by the angelic pair
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community; the angelic address of the weeping mourner is a stock scene-element
moves.paradigm: reported speech; angelic interlocutor

moves.label: M32
moves.paraphrase: The angels ask Mary — addressing her as 'woman' — why she is weeping.
moves.substrate: Mary (as addressee) and her weeping-state (as the presupposition being interrogated)
moves.outcome: an explanation of her weeping is elicited from Mary
moves.sitz: narrated scene inside the tomb; late 1st c. CE community's telling
moves.paradigm: solicitous / clarifying question to a mourner; opening move of a recognition-scene

moves.label: M33
moves.paraphrase: Mary responds to the angels with the following.
moves.substrate: the utterance-content she conveys to the angels (embedded moves M34 and M35)
moves.outcome: the angels receive Mary's reply
moves.sitz: late 1st c. CE Johannine community narrating Mary's reply, which is a near-repeat of her earlier report to the disciples (M5) but re-personalized ('my Lord', 'I do not know')
moves.paradigm: reported speech; grief-lament response to a solicitous question

moves.label: M34
moves.paraphrase: Some unspecified 'they' have taken Mary's Lord away.
moves.substrate: 'my Lord' (Jesus's body, re-personalized in Mary's own voice)
moves.outcome: the Lord is no longer where he was laid
moves.sitz: narrated scene inside/at the tomb; Mary re-states her own body-theft construal, now in the first-person-possessive ('my')
moves.paradigm: body-theft as the intuitive explanation; grief-personalization ('my')

moves.label: M35
moves.paraphrase: Mary herself does not know where the Lord's body has been put.
moves.substrate: the location of the Lord's body (the embedded LAY-move M36)
moves.outcome: the location remains opaque to Mary
moves.sitz: narrated scene inside/at the tomb; Mary's earlier 'we do not know' (M7) narrows to 'I do not know'
moves.paradigm: grief-search / where-is-the-body opacity; personalized

moves.label: M36
moves.paraphrase: The unspecified 'they' have laid the Lord's body in some place.
moves.substrate: the Lord's body ('him')
moves.outcome: the body is at some location unknown to Mary
moves.sitz: narrated scene inside/at the tomb; the presupposed act behind Mary's not-knowing
moves.paradigm: body-relocation scenario; grief-search
